**To:** Prof. Govind Prasad

**Subject:** Initial synthesis and benchmark results: Hazard3, Ibex, VeeR EL2 on SKY130
**Attachment:** initial_synthesis.pdf

Dear Sir,

Please find below our initial results for the three cores on SkyWater 130 nm. All three are
synthesized core-only (core plus a thin wrapper with identical ports, no memories or pads) with the
same open-source flow (LibreLane 3.0.17, Yosys, OpenROAD, sky130_fd_sc_hd standard cells), and
rv32imc_zicsr configurations with unused features disabled.

**1. Synthesis (SKY130, core-only)**

<!-- BEGIN collect.py:headline -->
| Core | Cells | Cell area (µm²) | Area vs Hazard3 | Flops | Pre-layout fmax estimate (MHz) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Hazard3 | 13,152 | 156,519 | 1.00× | 1,940 | 47.6 |
| Ibex (small) | 11,922 | 150,477 | 0.96× | 1,924 | 49.3 |
| VeeR EL2 (min) | 50,627 | 579,032 | 3.70× | 6,384 | 24.2 |
<!-- END collect.py -->

Area is standard-cell area after synthesis. VeeR EL2 is shown without its tightly-coupled
memories or caches and with its branch predictor off, to match Hazard3 and Ibex.

**2. Benchmarks in RTL simulation** (same binaries and compiler flags for every core, GCC `-O2`,
1-cycle memory; CoreMark checksums match the official values on all cores)

<!-- BEGIN collect.py:sim_email -->
| Core | Config | Tests passed | CoreMark/MHz | DMIPS/MHz | Published CoreMark/MHz | Measured / published |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hazard3 | default | 52/52 | 2.75 | 1.08 | 4.15 | 0.66 |
| Ibex | small | 52/52 | 2.23 | 0.83 | 2.47 | 0.90 |
| VeeR EL2 | no TCM (min) | 52/52 | 0.81 | 0.34 | 3.6 | 0.22 |
| VeeR EL2 | ICCM + DCCM (tcm) | 51/52 | 3.07 | 1.25 | 3.6 | 0.85 |
<!-- END collect.py -->

- Hazard3: the published figure ([source](https://github.com/Wren6991/Hazard3#rp2350)) uses
  bit-manipulation extensions, a faster multiplier, a branch predictor and tuned `-O3` flags; ours has none of these.
- Ibex: same "small" configuration as the published figure ([source](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex#configuration)); the gap is most likely `-O3 -funroll-all-loops` there versus `-O2` here.
- VeeR EL2: the published figure ([source](https://www.westerndigital.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/2019/2019-12-10-western-digital-brings-memory-closer-to-compute-with-new-risc-v-innovations)) is a vendor simulation, with VeeR's
  intended memory system; see point 3.

**3. VeeR EL2 finding.** Without its tightly-coupled memories (ICCM/DCCM), VeeR fetches every
instruction over its external bus and reaches only about a fifth of its published CoreMark/MHz
(see "Measured / published" above). With ICCM and DCCM enabled (simulation with behavioural
memories) it is <!-- BEGIN collect.py:veer_tcm_ratio -->3.8<!-- END collect.py -->× faster and close to the published figure. Our ASIC results use the version
without them for now.

**4. Limitations.** VeeR's configuration cannot remove its PMP unit (16 entries) or its debug
module, which partly explains its larger area. fmax is not reported yet: signed-off timing will come
from the full layouts. All details are in the attached report.

**5. Next steps.** SKY130 core-only layouts (RTL-to-GDS with DRC/LVS checks) are running now, then
the padded chip top with I/O pads, then FPGA (PYNQ) and SCL 180 nm.

We would be grateful for your guidance on a few points:

1. **VeeR memories:** should VeeR be compared without its tightly-coupled memories (same memory
   system as the other cores), with them (its intended configuration, adding SRAM area), or both?
2. **VeeR PMP/debug:** may we patch VeeR's RTL to remove its PMP unit and debug module, for a
   strictly like-for-like comparison, or should we report it as configured?
3. **SCL 180 nm:** how do we get access to the PDK, which tools does it support (open-source flow or
   Cadence), and may we use AI coding tools on the PDK files?
4. **I/O pads on SKY130:** should we build our own pad ring with the sky130_fd_io cells, or use the
   Caravel harness?

Thank you.

Regards,
